checks.explanation: Russia did gain territory in 2024 (roughly 1,600 square miles, about 20% of Ukraine occupied overall), but at an extremely high cost (an estimated 427,000 troops killed or injured that year) with no major strategic breakthrough, and the war ground on into 2025-2026 without a decisive Russian victory. 'Consolidating gains' is partly right, but the framing that Russia was clearly 'winning' and the stalemate narrative was 'a lie' is contestable given the casualty rate and lack of a knockout blow.

sources.title: Russia seized 1,600 square miles of Ukraine's territory in 2024 while losing 427,000 troops

checks.explanation: Netanyahu remained Israel's prime minister through the end of 2024 and continued in office well beyond, contrary to the prediction that he would be 2024's biggest political loser (implying a fall from power). Polling showing a desire for his ouster did not translate into an actual removal from office.

sources.title: A closer look at Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's consequential year

checks.explanation: TikTok/ByteDance did not go public in 2024, and remains privately held as of 2026, with no confirmed IPO timeline announced, contrary to the prediction.

sources.title: How to Invest in TikTok Stock in 2026

checks.explanation: OpenAI's valuation roughly doubled in 2024, rising from about $86 billion in January to $157 billion by October (and continuing to climb sharply in subsequent years), the opposite of the predicted decline. Secondary-share buyers at a $90B valuation ended up well in the money, not underwater.

sources.title: OpenAI closes funding at $157 billion valuation

checks.explanation: RFK Jr. was genuinely a major political story for most of 2024, polling as high as 13% in an independent bid, well above typical third-party candidates, but he suspended his campaign in August and endorsed Trump, ending the year more as a footnote than a 'winner.' Real story, but not a clean win by year's end.

sources.title: RFK Jr.: Is the substantial polling support for third-party candidates real?

checks.explanation: By October 2024, assessments concluded Israel's Gaza objectives were 'far from attainable' despite killing much of Hamas's top leadership, while the war produced a severe humanitarian crisis (over 42,000 killed per Gaza health authorities, about 2 million displaced, nearly 60% of buildings damaged, and roughly 1.95 million people facing severe food insecurity), matching the prediction closely.

sources.title: A year on, Israel's Gaza objectives far from attainable

checks.explanation: Several major commodities did boom in 2024 as predicted: gold and silver rose over 25%, cocoa surged 172%, coffee jumped nearly 70%, and natural gas rose 50%, even though the broad Bloomberg Commodity Index itself only gained modestly (about 2.9-5.1%) and oil/industrial metals underperformed, so the 'boom' framing holds for a meaningful chunk of the asset class even if not uniformly across it.

sources.title: Periodic Table of Commodity Returns Reveals Winners and Losers for 2024

checks.explanation: Anduril had a breakout 2024 largely driven by demand for systems like Roadrunner: its valuation reportedly reached the $14-30.5 billion range on roughly 138% year-over-year revenue growth, and the Pentagon awarded it a $250 million contract for 500 Roadrunner interceptors, with the product line booking over $350 million in orders, closely matching the prediction.

sources.title: Anduril lands $250 million Pentagon contract for drone defense system

checks.explanation: No dark-horse candidate emerged. Biden withdrew in July 2024 and Kamala Harris became the Democratic nominee without a contested primary; the general election was a straightforward Trump-vs-Harris race, which Trump won 312-226 in the electoral college, not a disruption by an outside candidate.

The opposite of this prediction occurred. NATO leaders declared Ukraine on an 'irreversible path' to membership at the July 2024 Washington Summit rather than letting membership prospects fade, and NATO allies provided over EUR 50 billion in aid in 2024 (exceeding their own EUR 40 billion baseline pledge), with the US separately providing a $20 billion loan late in the year, the opposite of fading US commitment.

sources.title: NATO promises Ukraine $43bn in aid, 'irreversible path' to membership

checks.explanation: The specific, most testable part of this prediction did not happen: there has been no settlement between the New York Times and OpenAI. The lawsuit remained unresolved and ongoing as of 2025 (with the Times spending $10.8 million on related litigation costs in 2024 alone), and instead of settling with OpenAI, the Times signed a separate licensing deal with Amazon.

sources.title: The New York Times v. Microsoft and OpenAI

checks.explanation: Germany's economy matched the prediction closely: it entered a second consecutive year of recession in 2024 (-0.2% GDP), the only G7 economy to contract that year, driven substantially by an automotive crisis as Chinese competitors like BYD took market share, with German brand sales falling sharply (BMW down 30%, Porsche down 19%, Mercedes down 13% in Q3 2024 alone).

sources.title: Germany: Europe's biggest economy is in crisis. Just look at Volkswagen

checks.explanation: Real but modest evidence, not a clean 'biggest winner' confirmation. Some bootstrapped AI-era startups did post striking capital efficiency (e.g. reaching seven-figure annual revenue with under $1 million raised), and AI-using startups reported somewhat higher profitability rates than non-AI ones (61% vs 54%), but this is a meaningful trend rather than a headline-level dominant story for 2024 specifically.

sources.title: Seed-Strapping: The New Playbook for Building Profitable AI Companies in 2024

checks.explanation: Vertical SaaS faced serious 2024 disruption as predicted: analysts described the category as 'heading toward a footnote in software history' as no-code tools displaced multiple vertical SaaS seats with a single license, and specific vertical players like ZoomInfo saw growth fall to near zero, matching the prediction closely.

sources.title: bye bye vertical saas, blame it on...

checks.explanation: Professional sports valuations did not peak in 2024; they kept climbing. The top 50 most valuable sports teams were worth over $353 billion in the 2025 ranking, up 22% from 2024 alone and more than double their value from four years earlier, directly contradicting the predicted 2024 peak.

sources.title: The World's 50 Most Valuable Sports Teams 2025 List
